questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The culture of Ireland, Trinity's good reputation the good reviews from students at UCPH

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, Trinity are very good at taking care of their visiting students

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had to swap courses, and they were very good at explaining how it was done and making it easy for me

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: We pretty easily found an Airbnb outside of town about 7 months before we went. It was however pretty expensive and the house was very cold. I recommend looking at student accommodations like Yugo as early as possible, as almost all available student accommodations were gone by March/April.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Dublin is pretty expensive. Some areas are nicer than others, especially if you don't live very near the center of the city, so doing some research into which area you're gonna live in is a good idea.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is no on campus housing available for Erasmus students

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You fill out a form online before coming stating which courses you would like. Once you arrive you have a week to try out courses and make changes if needed/wanted. If you choose any of the courses that the first year students have (like torts of constitutional law) you do not get to try them before having to decide if you want to switch courses. It is very easy to switch courses and Trinity are very good at informing the students about the process and important deadlines.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Trinity has a school of law and an Erasmus office, both of which are very good at helping with any questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes i had wanted before i went, and I got to switch one of the courses with another course i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to read about the exam information and amount of course work before choosing your course.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: At Trinity only undergraduate (BA) courses are offered to visiting students.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar, but the students are much more on their own. The readings for each class are a lot less organized but still somewhat manageable. The teaching is almost 100% the lecturer talking in front of a powerpoint to 35-70 students. There is only class discussion if the lecturer wants it, which was about 50/50.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Food Law, Commercial Law and Medical Law and Ethics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Medical Law and Ethics - very interesting deep dive into Irish medical law, with good exams and decent lecturers.

Food Law - EU focused course so UCPH students already know some of the information, very engaging and skilled lecturer, very good exams.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Enrolling in student societies costs money, ranging from 2 Euro to 25 Euro. It was almost always worth it paying the enrollment fee. The sports center on campus (gym, swimming pool, etc) costs 78 Euro for the whole semester.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Rent was more expensive than i thought
The bus was cheaper than i thought

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Trinity has a huge amount of sports clubs and social societies, ranging from boxing, kayaking, hiking, shooting and climbing, to movie club, nordic club, philosophic club and jazz club

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The Phil (philosophic society) - They have a lot of cool events and do debate training
The Law Society - Also very cool events and parties
The boxing club - Very friendly, good training 3 times a week, has space for people who are brand new and experienced

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Hiking in Howth
The pubs around Dublin
Galway and Cliffs of Moher
Glendalough

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The Irish people are very friendly and outgoing, so had to get used to strangers talking to me more than in Denmark

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Irish people are very friendly and great to be around.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Take part in the very active student environment, join clubs, join societies, go to the parties.
Go out and see the country outside Dublin, it is very beautiful.
Choose your exams wisely, having more essays means having more freedom to plan your stay however you choose.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to try out so many new things through the societies and clubs at Trinity

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having started my exam prep too late

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
